On Balanced Scales

In the synthetic tradition of balanced scales, the weight of each choice is measured against the weight of its twin. Scales must be kept level by the one who holds them. A holder who tips the scales in secret has broken the tradition. Open disclosure of the weights used is the central rule. The tradition speaks of three bowls: one for the actor, one for the affected, and one for the observer. A choice that cannot be shown to the observer is set aside. Reasons are placed on the scales in plain view.
